rejected.note: The section's title. What it names -- operation from a moving vehicle or aircraft -- is prohibited by ¶1 and its subparagraphs, which moving-vehicle-operation quotes. The title carries neither the prohibition nor the exception for a sparsely populated area.

The section's title, and in the 2020 text it reads 'Daylight operation' -- the amendment rewrote both the title and the rule. It states no permission and no condition: the prohibition on operating at night, and the civil-twilight allowance, are in the paragraphs beneath it, which night-operation quotes.

The section's title. The rule it names -- that the remote pilot in command, the visual observer and the person manipulating the controls must be able to see the aircraft with unaided vision -- is stated in (a) and (b), which visual-line-of-sight and unaided-visual-contact quote.

The section's title, naming the role. Every requirement that follows from using a visual observer is in ¶1's list, which visual-observer-conditions quotes; the title does not say whether one is required, and neither does the section.

The section's title. The single-aircraft rule it names is stated in ¶1, which single-aircraft quotes; in this baseline the sentence forbids operating more than one at a time rather than naming the flight-control manipulator. The title says 'multiple' where the rule states the limit.
The section's title. Both halves of this one-paragraph section -- the prohibition and the definition of hazardous material it makes for its own purposes -- are in ¶1, which hazardous-material quotes.

The section's title, and it names two things the section does state: the yielding rule in (a) and the well-clear rule in (b), quoted by right-of-way and well-clear. The semicolon in the title joins the two subjects and obliges nothing.
The section's title. The prohibition and the two classes of human being it excepts are in ¶1 and the subparagraphs beneath it, which over-human-beings quotes.
The section's title. Which airspace, and the ATC authorisation that makes operation in it lawful, are in ¶1, which airspace-authorized quotes. 'Certain airspace' names no class.
The section's title. The prohibition and the permission that lifts it are in ¶1, which restricted-area-permitted quotes.
The section's title, naming three things the section requires before flight. The list itself is in ¶1 and its subparagraphs, which preflight-actions quotes.

The section's title. Who the limitations bind is in the introductory text, which operating-limitations quotes, and the four limits are in (a) to (d), quoted by speed-limit, altitude-limit, visibility-minimum and cloud-clearance.
